Prevention: Only use certified seed to avoid introduction through contamination.
Clean equipment and farm machinery to prevent seeds being spread
Do not accept potentially contaminated materials, e.g. fill dirt, hay or soil
Control established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
Prepare the soil by turning under dry conditions to reduce infestations
Use water from a source free of the weed for watering and flooding
Before planting seed, prepare seed bed and wait for the first rain showers to promote weed germination then control by use of a post- emergent herbicde (glyphosphate) when weeds are 2-3 weeks old
Monitoring: Annual grass, spreading or stiffly erect, tufted or reclining at base; 0.3-2 m high.
Leaves dark green, linear and flat; 10−65 cm long and 5-30 mm wide.
Inflorescences branched, upright or nodding (10−25 cm long) with flowerheads ('branches', ca. 5cm long).
Regularly inspect fields, at least biweekly and in particular during and shortly after the wet season, and consider direct control when present
Look our for it in wetlands and along waterways.
Water and storm events can spread seeds
Direct Control: Flood rice fields with 15-22 cm of water, to prevent weeds developing, until the dough stage.
Flooding with 2-3 cm water will offer limited control
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Use glyphosate (2 lt/ha) before planting rice when there is a heavy infestation.
Satunil (40% thiobencarb w/w +propanil 20% w/w) or fenoxaprop.
Satunil at a rate of 2.5L/ha as a post emergent foliar application in the field
